title: Twoey dink vs no-spin and heavy slice (trimmed to 2:57)

clips.title: Title: The twoey dink
clips.line: Opening title over the first rally

clips.title: Heavy slice: open face, swing straight up, not forward
clips.line: “When they put spin on it, you lift it up… you can't flick it forward, go forward and it's in the net.”

clips.title: No spin: face ~20° closed, swing more forward
clips.line: “If I feed you a ball with no pace, then you add a little more power. Just like table tennis.”

clips.title: Hips lift the arm: stand up, make an arc
clips.line: “Use your hips to help lift the arm… stand up, don't move forward… make an arc.”

clips.title: Sidespin: angled face drops, square face goes up
clips.line: “It's already cutting sideways… close the face at an angle and it drops… meet it square and direct so it goes up.”

clips.title: Read the ball: two rules side by side
clips.line: “Your technique isn't the problem. The problem is how you meet the ball, at what moment, with which ball.”

notes: Timeline is the trimmed 2:57 cut (work/trimmed.mp4). Source cuts removed: 0:10.0–0:31.8, 1:35.0–1:51.7, 2:52.9–3:09.8, 3:52.5–end.
Paddle angles, swing paths and ball flights are schematic, not measured from the footage.
Quoted lines are English translations of the coach's Vietnamese; the English subtitles are burned into preview.mp4 only.
